text:
Alice M.: quick sync — i've pushed a PRD draft for a small "inference controls" playbook (batching, prefix/KV caching guidance, and quantization recommendations). need input on scope for an initial shippable slice.
Ben K.: skimmed. high level looks good. customers want per-route batch windows; is that in scope?
Alice M.: short answer: yes, per-route batching knobs + sane defaults. question is whether the PRD should include automatic SLO-driven tuning or manual-only in v1.
Carol S.: for enterprise customers i'm hearing they want deterministic latency. auto tuning could be risky initially. i'd prefer manual controls + logging/metrics for v1.
Dave R.: +1. we should include an acceptance criteria block that explicitly calls out fallback behavior when batch sizes spike latency.
Eva L.: customer ask: support for kv prefix caching invalidation rules — they have dynamic prompts with user-specific prefixes. any design notes?
Alice M.: added an edge-cases section in the doc about prefix collisions and TTL strategies. proposal: per-route cache namespace + optional per-request cache-bypass flag.
Ben K.: that works. on quantization: do we recommend int8 only or include a q4_0 suggestion? ops/infra impact matters (memory vs perf).
Carol S.: recommend graded profiles: "safe" (fp16), "cost" (int8), "aggressive" (q4 variants) with documented loss risk and perf numbers. keep automatic switching out of v1.
Dave R.: acceptance criteria proposal (draft):
```
- deploy a per-route batching config with default max_batch_ms=20 and max_batch_tokens=2048
- prefix cache: per-route namespace + ttl default 5m, ability to set bypass=true per request
- quant profiles documented + one validated model per profile on dedicated infra
- observability: per-request latency histogram, per-route cache hit/miss, batch size distribution
- graceful fallback: when 95th latency > SLO, route should fall back to smaller batch size or lower-quant model automatically (alert triggered)
```
Eva L.: problems to flag: cache invalidation complexity for multi-tenant prefixes, billing accuracy for cached tokens, and model quality regressions from quantization.
Alice M.: noted. for launch gating: propose gated beta with 3 pilot customers, 2 small/1 mid-market, and a rollback playbook.
Ben K.: timeline ask: is this Q2 min shippable? can we scope to manual-only tuning + telemetry to hit Q2?
Carol S.: yes, manual controls + telemetry + docs should be doable if eng + infra allocate 3 sprints. ops needs a simple runbook.
Dave R.: i'll draft the rollback/runbook and the small infra changes. pete from infra will need to approve kernel/quant infra tests.
Alice M.: action items: 1) ben and carol to finalize acceptance criteria in PRD by EOD Fri; 2) dave to author rollback/runbook; 3) eva to assemble customer pilot list; 4) me to update PRD with edgecases and per-route API examples.
Ben K.: noted. also adding a tiny example for API shapes:
```json
POST /v1/infer?route=chat-recs
{
  "prompt": "...",
  "inference_controls": {"batching": {"max_batch_ms": 15}, "cache": {"namespace": "route:chat-recs", "bypass": false}, "quant_profile": "cost"}
}
```
Eva L.: I'll ping customer success for pilots, tagging @carol for enterprise constraints. :mag_right: 
ops-bot: reminder — please include monitoring dashboards in the PRD; infra policy requires coverage for any new per-route config.
Alice M.: thanks — i'll fold that in. any objections to shipping manual-only controls + docs as v1 and a plan for automated SLO-driven tuning in v2?
Carol S.: no objections. :) :thumbsup:
Ben K.: no objections. go ahead.
Dave R.: sounds good. i'll drop a short RFC for the fallback logic by Monday.
Alice M.: great — will update PRD and ping for a final read before EOD Friday. thanks everyone.
